text:
Dear Dr. Henderson,

Thank you for agreeing to evaluate Clara Jenkins, a 57-year-old accountant with an unknown age of onset, who presents with recurrent, painful spasmodic contractions and cramping of her calf muscles. 

She is otherwise healthy, takes only a daily multivitamin, does not smoke, and has no family history of neuromuscular disease.

On physical examination, she demonstrates no loss of ambulation, walking with a normal, unassisted gait. Detailed motor testing revealed 5/5 strength throughout, with no proximal upper limb muscle weakness, no distal upper limb muscle weakness, no proximal lower limb muscle weakness, and no distal lower limb muscle weakness. Specifically, there was no foot dorsiflexor weakness. Inspection revealed no distal lower limb amyotrophy and no fasciculations. Exteroceptive sensation was normal to both light touch and pinprick. Deep tendon reflexes showed no decreased patellar reflex and no absent patellar reflexes, with bilateral knee jerks graded 2+. Her Achilles responses were definitely diminished, eliciting 1+ bilaterally, though an absent Achilles reflex was not observed.

Investigations revealed that circulating creatine kinase activity was not elevated. On electrodiagnostic evaluation, there was no decreased compound muscle action potential amplitude and sensory nerve conduction velocity was not abnormal; EMG showed no neuropathic changes. A prior skeletal muscle biopsy demonstrated pronounced grouping of histochemical fiber types, but showed no muscle fiber atrophy, no angulated muscle fibers, and no rimmed vacuoles. Finally, a transthoracic echocardiogram was unremarkable, showing no left ventricular hypertrophy.

I would be most grateful for your clinical impression and advice on further management.

Sincerely,
Dr. Arthur Vance
